newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CULLINAN STEERS S.AFRICA TO YET ANOTHER WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CULLINAN STEERS S.AFRICA TO YET ANOTHER WIN.

text.p: Daryll Cullinan hit a stylish 85 not out to steer South Africa to an emphatic six-wicket win in the first of seven one-day internationals against Australia on Saturday

Needing 224 for victory, South Africa reached their target with three overs to spare after Cullinan and Jacques Kallis had put on 122 for the fourth wicket from the precarious position of 50 for three in the 13th over.
Kallis was well stumped by Adam Gilchrist for 63 from 81 balls but Cullinan stayed to the end, striking nine fours in a 112-ball stay.
Tigerish South African fielding had earlier precipitated an alarming Australian batting collapse after Hansie Cronje won the toss and put the tourists in.
Stuart Law and Steve Waugh both made 50 during a third wicket stand of 97, but from 129 for two Australia lost seven wickets for 49 runs.

Law pulled off spinner Pat Symcox to deep mid-wicket after reaching 50 from 65 deliveries with six fours and Waugh then became one of three run out victims as Herschelle Gibbs, Cronje and Jonty Rhodes all produced brilliant throws.
At 178 for nine, Australia's blushes were spared by their last pair who equalled a 17-year-old record by adding 45 for the tenth wicket.
Michael Bevan (51 not out) and 28-year-old Queensland fast bowler Adam Dale, making his debut, equalled the mark set by Trevor Laughlin and Max Walker at Sydney against England.
Bevan reached his tenth 50 in his 50th game from just 57 balls with three fours and a six, and Dale showed he may well bat higher in future with 15 not out on a slow but blameless surface.
South Africa have now won 35 of their last 40 one-day internationals while Australia have lost 13 out of 19 since their loss to Sri Lanka in the World Cup final.
